{"world_model":"Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.15–0.25 s) + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is roughly pixel-proportional, plus a memory-bound large-map component (BN/GELU/pool at 31×31, group 1 and the whitening output). Accuracy is a slowly rising function of total steps, about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, which costs about 1.5–2.7 s/pp.

Noise: 3-seed accuracy SE is about 0.1–0.15 pp. Held-out 10-seed SE is about 0.06 pp. Time noise is about ±0.03 s. Any change to RNG use (the step count) re-rolls the seeds 0–2 draw. Selection on seeds 3–12 carries a winner's curse of roughly 0.05–0.1 pp.

Tip E033 (30/10/30/30 px split) has seeds 0–2 at 0.7536 and time 5.69 s. The held-out mean is near the 0.752–0.753 margin, so there is almost no headroom.

Mechanisms I believe:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033), and the 32 px tail carries accuracy (E018, E011, E024).
2. Backward truncation and sample dropping save more than their MAC share because the work is memory-bound (E028 −0.5 s, E031 −0.6 s). The accuracy cost is about 0.1–0.3 pp, which is about the epoch-dial rate. E028 lost 0.2 pp on seeds 0–2 for −0.84 s, so freeze plus epochs is probably net positive but not hugely.
3. The averaging and LS settings (Lookahead alpha exponent, interval, two-stage LS) sit at a tuned optimum. Perturbations in either direction lost 0.3–0.7 pp (E025, E030, E032). Expect further averaging or LS tweaks to be null or negative.
4. wd ×0.5 gave about +0.2 pp (E016). Muon helped (E006). The epoch dial is roughly linear.
5. Systems work (CUDA graphs, E015) saves about 1%. Prepare overhead is about 0.1–0.2 s, partly removable.

Misses explained: I underestimated the time savings from memory-bound cuts and from early low resolution. I overestimated how much averaging and LS tuning could add.

The accuracy cost is about 0.1–0.3 pp, which is about the epoch-dial rate. E028 lost 0.2 pp on seeds 0–2 for −0.84 s, so freeze plus epochs is probably net positive but not hugely.
3. The averaging and LS settings (Lookahead alpha exponent, interval, two-stage LS) sit at a tuned optimum. Perturbations in either direction lost 0.3–0.7 pp (E025, E030, E032). Expect further averaging or LS tweaks to be null or negative.

forecasts.reason: The freeze saves about 0.5 s and 0.5 epoch adds about 0.3 s. Accuracy is about neutral, near the keep gate, so the outcome is a coin flip.
Bit-identical systems work should save about 0.03–0.1 s and leave accuracy unchanged, apart from non-determinism.

The whitening bias already stops after 3 epochs, but 3 epochs is about 34% of 8.75 epochs, so only the stop point would move. A small saving of about 1–2% is possible, but the detach adds graph variants.
A longer freeze saves more time and loses about 0.1–0.2 pp, so it sits near the gate.
This is a diagnostic. Fresh seeds should regress to roughly 0.753, slightly below the selected held-out mean.
Folding BN saves some memory traffic, but the complexity and the small train/eval mismatch risk make the net gain uncertain.
A diagnostic with no recipe change. It likely shows non-GEMM kernels taking 30% or more of a step.
Muon is probably worth about 0.3–0.6 pp over SGD, with time falling about 3%.

cruxes: Does the E028 freeze's accuracy cost (about 0.2 pp on seeds 0–2) hold on held-out seeds, and can +0.5 epoch recover it at about +0.3 s?
Is the tip's true population mean at or above 0.752, so that further trims are safe, or is it already below the bar?
How much of the remaining step time is memory-bound at 31×31 versus GEMM, and does it transfer to the PCIe judge?
